subject: AtlasPay: hosted API response degradation - customer communication & commitments
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@atlaspay.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observed partial-generation degradations affecting AtlasPay (initial detection)

Hi team,

We started seeing an elevated rate of partial/empty responses from the hosted generation path affecting a subset of AtlasPay requests at ~08:55 PDT. Traffic is concentrated in the us-west region and appears correlated with higher-than-normal KV-cache eviction churn on older model variants.

Initial notes: 
- Error class: partial generation / truncated payloads (clients receive status 200 with incomplete transcript)
- Impact window (detected): 08:55 - ongoing, elevated between 08:55-09:05 for ~0.6% of AtlasPay requests
- Observed p95 latency increase for affected sessions and higher retry rate from client SDKs

I’ve opened an incident on the status page (link below) and flagged AtlasPay in the customer impact list. I’m escalating to account and SRE to coordinate a customer communication.

Immediate ask from me: Sergio / Laura, can you reach out to AtlasPay Ops with an acknowledgement and the brief mitigation we can apply (variant fallback to a larger KV budget + temporary route to dedicated pool if they have dedicated traffic)? Ben, can you and SRE validate whether the eviction pressure is due to a rollout or a traffic pattern shift so we have a clear statement.

Attachments: small log snippet included (ops_log_snippet.txt)

Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-09-14-hosted-api-degradation

Thanks,
Evelyn
Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Maya Chen <maya.chen@atlaspay.com>, ops@atlaspay.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: AtlasPay: hosted API response degradation - customer communication & commitments

Hi Maya / AtlasPay Ops,

Thanks for the patience — wanted to acknowledge we detected an issue that may cause partial or truncated responses for a subset of your requests to our hosted text-generation API. We are actively investigating and have these immediate actions in place: 

- Mitigation applied: we routed affected AtlasPay requests to a variant with a larger KV-cache allocation to reduce eviction churn and enabled a short-lived prefetch buffer. This change was applied at 09:25 PDT and has reduced the error rate in our sampling.
- Status page: we posted an incident update with timeline and impact: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-09-14-hosted-api-degradation
- Next steps: our SRE team is validating root cause (eviction pressure vs. kernel scheduling contention). If needed, we can offer a temporary dedicated routing policy while we finalize fixes.

We understand partial responses are disruptive; our priority is restoring steady, reliable inference for you. I’ve cc’d our SRE and product leads (Evelyn, Ben, Laura) so they can share a technical summary and ETA for a permanent fix.

Would you prefer we switch your traffic to the temporary dedicated routing (if you have that capacity) or continue on the patched hosted variant while we finish the postmortem? If you can share any critical windows for you today, we’ll avoid making disruptive changes in flight.

Attachment: ops_log_snippet.txt (contains sanitized request IDs and cache metrics sample)

Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Maya Chen <maya.chen@atlaspay.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: AtlasPay: hosted API response degradation - customer communication & commitments

Thanks, Sergio — appreciate the quick update and the mitigation.

We had a handful of user-visible errors across payment verification flows this morning between 08:58–09:10 PDT. Moving to a temporary dedicated route sounds OK if it’s low-risk and reversible; we don’t have a scheduled deploy or big batch jobs for the rest of the day. Please proceed if your SREs recommend it.

Also, can you confirm what you’re planning for credits/contract remedies if we see downstream impact on transactions? We’ll need that to brief finance and operations.

-Maya
Maya Chen
Ops Lead, AtlasPay
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Cc: maya.chen@atlaspay.com
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-incident follow-up: AtlasPay hosted API partial-response event (summary & next steps)

Team — following up with the summary I sent AtlasPay and an internal action/commit list. This will live on the incident page and our internal postmortem doc, but I wanted to capture the customer-facing commitments here.

Summary:
- Incident window: 2026-09-14 08:55–09:40 PDT (peak impact 08:55–09:10)
- Root cause (preliminary): KV-cache eviction churn triggered by a model-variant rollout combined with a short-lived traffic spike; eviction pressure caused increased partial response rate for sessions relying on small cache allocations.
- Remediation taken: Variant fallback with increased KV budget (09:25 PDT), short-lived prefetch buffer, and selective routing to a dedicated warm pool for AtlasPay (applied 09:40 PDT).
- Customer impact: ~0.6% of requests for AtlasPay during the window experienced truncated payloads; AtlasPay reported user-visible errors in payment verification flows for a subset of customers.

Customer commitments made:
- Offer: discretionary service credit equivalent to one day of typical inference usage for the impacted endpoints; Sergio to coordinate the credit approval with Finance.
- Timeline: public postmortem scheduled for 2026-09-24 (internal draft due 2026-09-21).
- Technical: SRE to deliver a mitigation playbook for KV eviction events and model rollout guardrails by 2026-09-21.

Open internal actions: 
1) Ben / SRE: finalize kernel scheduling and eviction analysis. Deliverable: root cause write-up (due 2026-09-21).
2) Laura / Product: propose rollout guardrails to prevent low-KV variants from receiving traffic during high-churn windows (due 2026-09-21).
3) Sergio: coordinate credit approval with Finance and confirm with AtlasPay by 2026-09-18.
4) Evelyn: attach sanitized logs to the internal postmortem (ops_log_snippet.txt) and add trace ids to the incident page.

Maya (cc’d) — we’ve proposed the credit and timeline above; please reply if you need a faster cadence or have other expectations.

Thanks everyone,
Sergio
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
